To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relative contributions of different types of data vary across different levels of severity and that verbal protocols provide the bulk of the data.

(1) The relative value of different empirical sources of data depends on the type and severity of the problems uncovered; (2) The relative value depends on the specific usability study; (3) Verbal protocols are a rich source of evidence, but are not the only source; and (4) More work is needed to better understand the relative value of various types of evidence.

(1) verbal protocol data provided the sole source for more than one-third of the most severe usability problems uncovered by our study and more than two-thirds of the less severe usability problems; (2) although verbal protocol data provided more evidence than any other source, it did not contribute disproportionately to the more severe usability problems; and (3) the relative value of verbal protocol data is not known and should be studied further.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to evaluate an interface in order to identify its problems and how to prioritize these problems.
the question of how much evidence is needed for a usability problem to be considered valid.
understanding the value of empirical data in usability testing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the verbal protocol provided a substantial amount of the evidence, but the other data sources provided evidence for some of the most severe usability problems.
the verbal protocol was the best single source of evidence for the most severe problems uncovered by this study.
the verbal protocol is a valuable tool in usability testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

verbal protocol analysis provides the best source of information for uncovering usability problems and that the combination of verbal protocol analysis with other empirical data provides a more complete picture of usability problems.
the verbal protocol is the best source of evidence in a usability study.
, although the verbal protocols provided the most evidence for the problems, the questionnaires provided the most evidence of severity for these problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the verbal protocol is not the only source of evidence for usability problems.
different sources of empirical data contribute differentially to the discovery of usability problems.
the verbal protocol should not be considered as a single source of evidence, but rather as a source of evidence with its own strengths and weaknesses.
